about: Before/after text for rule changes in the record, for /eci-files/rules (docs/eci-files/PHASE5-SPEC.md section 4). Each side carries its own text status. 'verbatim': copied from the document itself (or an unaltered reproduction, named in note). 'quoted in reporting': the exact wording as a news report quotes it; the document itself was not seen. 'paraphrased from reporting': a report's description, not the document's wording. text_status is the weaker of the two sides. excerpt: true means lines outside the change were left out. Nothing here is reconstructed wording.

diffs.title: Rule 93: which election papers are open to public inspection
diffs.after_label: Rule 93(2) as amended by S.O. 5517(E), 20 Dec 2024
before: (2) Subject to such conditions and to the payment of such fee as the Election Commission may direct, -
(a) all other papers relating to the election shall be open to public inspection; and
(b) copies thereof shall on application be furnished.
after: (2) Subject to such conditions and to the payment of such fee as the Election Commission may direct, -
(a) all other papers as specified in these rules relating to the election shall be open to public inspection; and
(b) copies thereof shall on application be furnished.
diffs.note: The 'after' text applies the Gazette's amending instruction word for word: 'after the word “papers”, the words “as specified in these rules” shall be inserted'. The Gazette prints no consolidated rule. The Hindi text of the same notification places the phrase after 'संबंधित' ('relating'), not after 'papers'. The 'before' text is from Indian Kanoon's copy of the 1961 Rules, not a Gazette copy.

diffs.title: Who selects the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners
diffs.document: Anoop Baranwal judgment (2 Mar 2023), operative direction I, and Section 7 of the 2023 Act
diffs.before_label: Supreme Court's interim rule, 2 Mar 2023 until Parliament legislated
diffs.after_label: Section 7, CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023 (in force 2 Jan 2024)
before: I. We declare that as far as appointment to the posts of Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners are concerned, the same shall be done by the President of India on the basis of the advice tendered by a Committee consisting of
the Prime Minister of India,
the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and, in case, there is no such Leader, the Leader of the largest Party in the Opposition in the Lok Sabha having the largest numerical strength,
and the Chief Justice of India.
This norm will continue to hold good till a law is made by the Parliament.
after: 7. (1) The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall be appointed by the President on the recommendation of a Selection Committee consisting of—
(a) the Prime Minister—Chairperson;
(b) the Leader of Opposition in the House of the People—Member;
(c) a Union Cabinet Minister to be nominated by the Prime Minister—Member.

Explanation.—For the purposes of removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that where the Leader of Opposition in the House of the People has not been recognised as such, the leader of the single largest party in opposition of the Government in the House of the People shall be deemed to be the Leader of Opposition.

(2) The appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall not be invalid merely by reason of any vacancy in or any defect in the constitution of, the Selection Committee.
diffs.note: The 'before' lines are one sentence of the majority's direction I, split at its list items. The 'after' text is clause 7 of the bill as introduced. The government's notice of amendments of 11 Dec 2023 proposes no change to clause 7, and the opposition amendment to put the CJI back was negatived (selection-law-rs-passes-bill). The quote on selection-law-rule-selection-committee matches clause 7(1)(c). The India Code copy of the Act could not be fetched for this check; confirm against it before launch.

diffs.title: How the three Commissioners decide: 1991 Act and 2023 Act
diffs.document: Section 10 of the 1991 Act and Section 18 of the 2023 Act
diffs.before_label: Section 10, Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991
diffs.after_label: Section 18, CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023
before: (1) The Election Commission may, by unanimous decision, regulate the procedure for transaction of its business as also allocation of its business amongst the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
(2) Save as provided in sub-section (1), all business of the Election Commission shall, as far as possible, be transacted unanimously.

(3) Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), if the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners differ in opinion on any matter, such matter shall be decided according to the opinion of the majority.
after: (1) The Election Commission may, by unanimous decision, regulate the procedure for transaction of its business as also allocation of its business amongst the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

(2) All business of the Election Commission shall, as far as possible, be transacted unanimously, and if the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners differ in opinion on any matter, such matter shall be decided according to the opinion of the majority.
diffs.note: The 2023 text is clause 17 of the bill as introduced. The government's notice of amendments proposes no change to it, and it became Section 18 when new clause 15A (now Section 16) was inserted. Sub-section (1) is unchanged; the old sub-sections (2) and (3) are merged. Confirm against the India Code copy of the Act before launch.

diffs.title: Online Form 6 on ECINET: the added 'last SIR' question
diffs.document: Form 6 (application for inclusion of name), online version on ECINET
diffs.before_label: Form 6 as prescribed in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 (last amended 17 Jun 2022)
diffs.after_label: Online Form 6 on ECINET, as seen by The Indian Express on 11 Jul 2026
before: No question about the last SIR roll.
The applicant gives the name and EPIC number of family members with whom they currently reside.
after: A “declaration form” part, not lettered, inserted between parts J and K.
my name exists in Electoral Roll of last SIR
my parents name (Father, Mother, Grandfather, Grandmother) exists in the electoral roll of last SIR
neither my name nor my parents name exists in the electoral roll of last SIR
For either of the first two options: the Assembly constituency, booth number and serial number in the last SIR roll.
diffs.note: Neither side is from a primary document. The statutory Form 6 could not be fetched: the ECINET portal serves only the 2022 Form 6 guidelines at voters.eci.gov.in/guidelines/Form-6_en.pdf, not the form. The 'before' lines paraphrase The Indian Express's description of the statutory form. The three options on the 'after' side are the portal's wording as The Indian Express quoted it; the other 'after' lines paraphrase its report. The online form sits behind a login and could not be opened. The report says the question was not marked mandatory, but the form could not be submitted without answering it. The Indian Express reported it was still on the portal on 21 Sep 2026.
